name: (none)
role: Not yet given a real state - `class_counter` (`+0x2E`) only increments "for every unit whose state is not 0" (see the unit record), consistent with 0 meaning "just allocated, not yet dispatched" rather than an ordinary idle state. Also doubles as the dispatch convention's own "no transition this tick" sentinel: every per-turn case below returns a next-state byte, and the shared caller only runs the actual state-transition pair when that byte is nonzero - so a case "returning 0" just means "stay put", not literally jumping to state 0. **`+0xC` bit `0x40000000`, generalized this session**: appears throughout this catalog (states 19/26/32/34/36/37/38/39/41/42/43 and others) as a mysterious "pose-variant"/"water-sink" bit tested at the top of a sub-state handler - tracing ~180 of its SETTER sites (not just the test sites) resolves it: it is NOT state- or water-specific at all. It is the generic "my own `+0x2D` SUB-STATE field was just (re)assigned" marker, set in lockstep with every `mov [unit+0x2D],N` across the whole exe - both by `order_execute`'s own 31 order-kind handlers (which reuse `+0x2D` as their OWN internal step counter while a person is in state 10) and by every person-state handler's own internal sub-state machine. A sub-state handler testing this bit at entry is simply asking "was I just switched into this sub-state this tick (need one-time setup) or am I continuing it (skip setup, just tick down)" - completely generic, reused by whichever system currently owns the unit's `+0x2D` field. The "save/exit old state" step of the person-STATE transition pair itself (`0x4ED6F0`, see functions.tsv's own row) is a confirmed no-op and does NOT set this bit - it is set by the higher-level order/sub-state-assigning code instead, orthogonal to `+0x2C` state transitions.

name: idle hand-off
role: Initial state for a person with no active behaviour yet; on an RNG-timed expiry hands off to its own per-type ongoing default via table 0x5A7064 (wildman -> 8, angel -> 28, everyone else -> 10). See "Idle behaviour: the idle hand-off: state 1, then state 10".

name: drowning
role: Entered from the universal life-step when the fine-grained per-pixel drowning check (0x4EEFF0) is true. Per-turn body 0x4D5B60 plays the drown sound/effect (0x4EEC80), jitters the facing (+0x57) by a random offset and swims (0x4E6A70, 40-tick duration), redraws (0x4EE580), then calls 0x4EF140 (own functions.tsv row) with the per-type pair 0x5A706A (sink rate)/0x5A706C (kill depth): 0 = keep drowning, no transition (still afloat, not yet past the depth); 1 = resurface to the per-type default (table 0x5A7064, same debug/shaman override as elsewhere) - fires the instant `is_land_at` says there's solid support again, regardless of how far already sunk; 2 = drown outright to state 3 (death), life forced to exactly 0 (not a subtraction). **Confirmed this session**: every person type checked (wildman through angel) has the identical -16/turn, -256-deep table pair - a flat 16-turn (1.33 s) kill from first going under, no per-type variation - and this is the SAME mechanism a person blown into open water by Blast goes through (pop3-rev-analysis.md "Drowning", "Blast push and flight" - 3 live-observed cases already matched -16/turn, 16 turns, -256, forced-to-0 exactly), not a separate blast-specific mechanic as an earlier pass of the spec assumed.

name: death

name: tumbling / ground recovery
role: NOT the airborne ballistic flight itself (no velocity/height field +0x49/+0x4B/+0x4D/+0x41 is read anywhere in this function - that physics runs in the separate universal per-unit step, 0x4E6D1D/0x4E6D6D) - this is the GROUND recovery choreography that follows it, confirmed live (a tribe-1 brave hit by Blast enters this state the instant BLOWN, +0xC bit 0x80000, is set). Own sub-state (+0x2D) is a 0/1/2 arrival check (48-unit then 216-unit thresholds against a reference position, meaning unconfirmed) feeding an 8-way jump table (sub-states 3-10): picks a clear nearby cell via an 8-direction offset table (0x895ED9, default 0x895EF1) and moves there (0x4E9DD0); waits randomized timers (+0x70, 4-31 turns, LCG 0x89D178). **The "is this candidate spot OK" check, 0x4D5420, is now traced and confirmed NOT building-aware**: it walks the cell's own linked list (0x8A03E4) filtering strictly for class-1 (person) entries, checking only per-type terrain-climbability (WALK_ALT_DIFF2, movement-profile table 0x5A7B90+0x10, same field state 33 uses) and collision with another live person already claiming the same spot - a building (class 2) on that cell is simply invisible to this check. The sibling function in the initial arrival dispatch, 0x4D5120, is more involved and surfaces one new unconfirmed lead: a per-CELL linked-list HEADER flag (`[cell_list_head+0x1]` bit 0x2, not a per-object field) that, when set, triggers a re-place via 0x4044B0 - plausibly "this cell holds something solid" (a building footprint is the obvious guess, not confirmed). **Resolved, same session, by tracing the physics/landing step itself (0x4E6D00/ground() 0x44E940, see functions.tsv's own rows)**: landing on a building gets no special handling at all - ground() is a pure terrain-height interpolation with no building/class check, so a thrown person always lands at raw terrain height on that cell regardless of any building there; there just isn't a building-awareness mechanism anywhere in this whole chain. **Correction: +0x78 is NOT a trailing-effect counter (an earlier pass of this row wrongly equated it with state 26's own +0xA4 counter) - the Reference already documents +0x78 as a person's plain CARRIED WOOD amount.** The two checks on it here (threshold <1) just pick the matching Idle/Walk vs. holding-wood/Walk-with-wood pose pair (see animation note below); separately, once the first wait timer expires with wood still carried, it spawns a class-5 type-0xB debris effect once per exactly 100 wood decremented from +0x78 (one standard wood load) until 0 - reads as dropping/spilling carried wood in a puff per load while settling, not a generic effect burst (the same +0x78-by-100 pattern also appears in state 41, own row, and in "Preacher conversion"'s sub-state 4 - the same wood-drop mechanic in all three places). NOT ACTUALLY OBSERVED LIVE: the one live trial never logged +0x78/wood, so whether this branch (holding-wood pose, wood-drop puffs) fired for that specific brave is unknown - needs a wood-carrying brave specifically. Every 32 turns while grounded, two more LCG rolls can kick it back into sub-state 6 (~13/32) or 10 (~3/64), both also setting flags+0xC bit 0x40000000 (the same bit cheat.md's live drowning trace found on entering the water-sink sequence, and state 37, own row, toggles repeatedly - looks like a general pose-variant bit, not confirmed water-exclusive) - this randomness is why live substates wander non-monotonically (4→5→10→5→6→7…) instead of counting through a fixed sequence. Sub-state 7 ("getting up") rerolls a fresh facing/timer before looping back. Exit: two epilogues return the per-type default state via the same table 0x5A7064 state 1 (0x4D3386) uses, one a fixed state 0x27 (39, shaman debug-mode override, same pattern as 0x518560). **Cross-system note, traced this session**: this state's own entry trigger (BLOWN, `+0xC` bit `0x80000`, set) and the in-FIGHT stagger/push (person_states state 25's stance 7, `fight_turn`/`0x518FB0`'s own row) are the SAME physics mechanism - a fight-stagger sets this exact bit too, and `fight_turn`'s own "has this fighter landed yet" check (`+0xE` bit `0x8`) is byte-aligned shorthand for this same `+0xC` bit `0x80000` DWORD, not a separate flag. So "waking up" from a fight knockback is the in-combat counterpart to this state's own "wait for BLOWN to clear, then recover" trigger - same signal, different owner (the fight controller's own stance field vs. this person state). Ghidra's function range for 0x4D73E0 (claimed end 0x4D80B9) is wrong - 0x4D7FD0 inside that range is actually the death/spirit-rise record push (state 3's own mechanism), a separate function. **Animations resolved this session, directly from the exe's static data (0x5A6D50/0x5A6858, "Fight"'s own `[action×9+type]` table at 0x4D3FF0, cross-checked against 7 already-known action values, all matching)**: no dedicated "down" sprite - calls 0x4D3FF0 with actions 1/5 (already-documented Walk/Walk-with-wood, picked by the +0x78 wood check above) while moving to the picked spot, and 0/4 while settling, resolving to plain Idle (action 0, VSTART 6/53) and VSTART 10 ("standing still, holding wood", brave-specific, action 4, likewise wood-gated) - both already named in open-populous animations.md. So this whole recovery window most likely looks like an ordinary idle/standing (or holding-wood, if carrying any) person that just isn't taking orders, plus a few dropped-wood puffs if it had wood - not a visibly prolonged "struggling on the ground" animation. This static table-reading is independently cross-checked against 7 already-known action values (all matched exactly) but NOT itself confirmed against this specific live trial. See open-populous pop3-rev-analysis.md "Tumbling and ground recovery" / "A blasted person fighting back". **Idle 'bored' poses (traced 2026-11-13): sub-state 5 is the plain standing-idle loop (object from action 0/4). Every 32 turns (`class_counter`&0x1F==0, 2.7 s) it rolls the 0x89D178 LCG twice: `rnd&0x1F > 0x12` (13/32) -> sub-state 6 (a short wander: picks a facing, timer 4..31 turns as sub-state 7, then back to 5), then `rnd&0x3F > 0x3C` (3/64, overrides the first) -> sub-state 10, the bored pose (case 0x4D7D06): brave -> object 0xA1 (VSTART 89, scratching), warrior -> 0xA2 (VSTART 91, push-ups), firewarrior -> 0xA3 (VSTART 90, push-ups), warrior/firewarrior only if `+0x82`&0xF0 <= 0x10 (meaning unknown); every other type gets no pose and drops straight back to 5. Duration timer `+0x70` = (draw-class byte +3 at 0x5A6AF8 stride 11, +1) x frame count of VSTART 89 (global 0x5A6ADC, used for all three types) + 1, i.e. one animation loop; the pose also ends early, reverting to the idle object, when the animation reaches its last frame. Memoryless: no idle-time threshold, 3/64 per 2.7 s check -> mean ~683 turns (~57 s), median ~39 s, can fire at the first check. Spy juggling (VSTART 92, object 0xA4) is NOT set here - not located.**

name: the conversion roll
role: The preacher-conversion CANDIDATE's own state while a roll is in progress (the striker is resolved via the candidate's own `+0x89`). Full preconditions, the success path (kill-and-replace, not a tribe-byte flip), and the roll-failure sub-state (0-6) "being preached to" choreography are all traced and live-confirmed - see "Preacher conversion" in pop3-rev-analysis.md. Explicitly excluded from the firewarrior/angel ranged-attack scan (0x51D0B0) and the Angel of Death's hunting AI (0x4DB980), but NOT excluded from the generic melee attacker-eligibility path (0x51C4C0) - confirmed live, a candidate can be pulled straight into pre-fight (29) or death (3) by an ordinary attacker. **States 32/42 (own rows, traced this session) also read a +0x89 reference field and are the leading candidates for the STRIKER's own counterpart state while this is in progress - not confirmed.** **Resolved, 2026-11-06**: the long-open "is state 23 reachable only by preacher/firewarrior candidates, contradicting `open-populous`'s own `may_preach` (ordinary followers only)" question is settled - see `functions.tsv`'s `0x43ABF0` row's same-day correction. The table-`0x5A7090` byte values that row originally quoted (used to gate who `preacher_strike_scan` can push into this state) were simply mis-read; re-read three independent ways this session, the real eligible-type set is brave/warrior/spy/firewarrior (type bit `0x20` SET), NOT preacher/firewarrior, and wildman/preacher/shaman/angel are the ones excluded - consistent with, not contradicting, `may_preach`'s "ordinary followers, never preachers/shamans" model. **Four more residual questions traced this session (range/capacity, a claimed "halving flag" on the conversion check, a "soul flying" visual, and whether the preacher plays one pose or a sequence) - see `functions.tsv`'s `0x43C7A0` row for the full writeup.** Summary: no halving flag exists anywhere on this roll (it's a flat 1-in-5 LCG check against the fixed constant `0x5AA504`, never modified by any flag found); the scan that feeds this state (`preacher_strike_scan`) covers a 3x3 (or 5x5, if the striker started in a building doorway) grid of 256-unit cells and strikes only the first eligible candidate per call, with no found cap stopping a second, later-struck candidate from entering this SAME state 23 under the same still-active striker (unconfirmed live whether this ever actually happens); the dedicated conversion visual is an 8-tick "conversion flash" (effect state 45, class-7 type 0x3A) spawned only on a SUCCESSFUL roll, which teleport-tracks the brand-new replacement unit every tick rather than flying a path from the preacher (see `effect_states.csv` state 45); and the preacher's own body never selects among multiple poses for itself anywhere in the order handler (`0x43C7A0`) - only the listener's pose/prop is table-driven - consistent with a single fixed preaching pose, though the exact animation id that maps to is a separate, untraced rendering layer.

name: scorched by a blast (forced run, "panics")
handler: 0x4D3832 (per-turn), 0x4D2D74 (entry, in `init_unit_class_1`/0x4D2740's own per-state ENTER dispatch, `switchD_004d290b` caseD_1a)
role: **Correction to this row's own earlier pass, same investigation thread, continued**: the previous note ("purely cosmetic... no movement") checked only the per-turn TICK body (0x4D3832, which does just play the ambient-crackle sound 0x51 and count down the trailing-effect visual) and missed that `init_unit_class_1` (0x4D2740) has a SEPARATE per-state ENTER dispatch (`switchD_004d290b`, the same two-dispatch architecture already confirmed for class 10 in `init_unit_class_10`/0x500E20's own row) - its case 0x1a (state 26) runs ONCE on entry and: sets a per-type cosmetic prop (`0x4D4040`, table `0x5A6F12`) and clears selection/pairing flags (`0x445750(0,0,self)` - exhaustively traced this session, see state 31's own row: only touches `+0x7A`/`+0x14` selection bits and UI-selection globals, confirmed NOT order/queue-related), sets speed `+0x5F = 0x6E` (110), sets the duration timer `+0x70 = 0x40` (64 turns), then rolls a fresh random heading via the standard `0x89D178` LCG and writes it to the facing field `+0x57` (masked to `0x7FF`, 0-2047), also setting `+0xC` bits `0x80`/`0x1000` (the same two bits "on fire"/state 31's own entry (`0x4D8FC0`, see that row) sets, and the SAME pair the generic helper 0x4D68C0 (states 4/13) and state 43 also set - a shared, reused "forced random movement" flag pair, not exclusive to panic). **This is a real, confirmed, code-level "runs at a random heading at speed 110 for 64 turns" effect** - almost exactly open-populous pop3-rev-analysis.md's old uncited "Panic (person state 0x1A)" description, just not a separate state from "scorched by a blast", not literally called that in any symbol, and with no scream sound found anywhere (only the ambient crackle, sound.tsv 0x51) - "screaming" in the old claim is unconfirmed/likely wrong. **Gating, confirmed by direct comparison**: entry via the blast-push code (`0x50B740`, `test BYTE PTR [+0x7A],0x1`) only fires this for a pushed person when the BLAST INSTANCE's own `+0x7A` bit 0x1 is set -
